professor: This week we are discussing homework. Some educators argue that homework helps students practice and develop discipline. Others think it adds stress without improving learning, especially for younger students. What is your view? Should schools give less homework?
posts: Aisha
I think schools should keep homework, but make it shorter. Practicing at home helps me remember what we did in class, but when I have three hours of homework, I just rush through it.
Marco
I'd go further and drop most homework. Students already spend six or seven hours at school. Time for sports, family and rest also matters for learning.

professor: Many companies now let employees work from home for part of the week. Do you think this is a positive change for workers and companies? Why or why not?
posts: Kenji
Working from home saves hours of commuting, and people can focus better without office noise. I think it's clearly positive.
Fatima
I see the benefits, but new employees miss out. They learn a lot just by sitting near experienced colleagues and asking quick questions.

professor: Some cities have banned cars from their centers on certain days. Supporters say this reduces pollution and makes streets safer. Critics say it hurts businesses and makes life harder for people who cannot walk long distances. Do you think car-free days are a good idea?
posts: Leo
Car-free days are great. When our city tried it, the air felt cleaner and families came out to walk and cycle.
Grace
My grandmother can't walk far, so on those days she just stays home. Any ban needs exceptions or better public transport.

professor: Social media lets people stay in touch with friends and family around the world. But some studies link heavy use to loneliness and anxiety. Overall, does social media do more to connect people or to isolate them?
posts: Omar
For me it connects. I moved abroad for university, and video calls and group chats keep me close to my family.
Sofia
I think it isolates many people. They scroll through others' perfect lives instead of spending time with friends in person.

professor: Some governments give free public transport to all residents. Supporters say it reduces traffic and helps people with low incomes. Others say the money would be better spent improving the service. Which approach do you prefer?
posts: Daniel
Free transport is a strong signal. If buses cost nothing, more people will leave their cars at home.
Mei
Free doesn't help if the buses are late and crowded. I'd rather pay a small fare for a service I can rely on.

professor: Many universities require students to complete community service before they graduate. Is this a good requirement, or should volunteering be a personal choice?
posts: Hannah
Required service introduces students to problems they'd never see otherwise. Many keep volunteering after they graduate.
Raj
If it's required, it isn't really volunteering. Students who are forced to do it often just count the hours.

professor: Artificial intelligence tools can now write essays and solve problems. Should students be allowed to use these tools for their coursework? Explain your view.
posts: Elena
Banning them is unrealistic. Schools should teach students to use them honestly, the way we learned to use calculators.
Tom
If students let a tool write their essays, they never learn to think through an argument themselves. Some limits are necessary.

professor: As cities grow, some build taller apartment buildings, while others expand outward with more houses. Which approach is better for a growing city, and why?
posts: Nadia
Building up is better. It protects farmland and makes public transport practical because more people live close together.
Chris
Many families want gardens and space. Expanding outward with good transport links gives them that choice.
